options.metric: sum of number_of_pedestrians_killed by calendar year of crash_date; counts pedestrian deaths, not crashes
options.denominator: not applicable; annual count, not a rate or share
options.reason: A line chart makes the progression of annual pedestrian death counts across calendar years easy to see.
options.interpretation: This framing answers the requested annual counts by summing number_of_pedestrians_killed across all police-reported NYC motor vehicle crash rows dated in each calendar year from 2013 through 2025; the plotted values are deaths, not crash counts. The line chart displays the annual totals in sequence, with each year’s exact count listed in the answer. A line chart is defensible because it makes the progression across calendar years visible while preserving the requested count for each year; it cannot count deaths outside police-reported crashes or independently verify recorded deaths. The check covered 2,132,218 in-range crash rows and found 0 missing crash dates, 0 missing pedestrian-killed values, 0 candidate default dates, and observed date endpoints spanning January 1 to December 31 in every year; all in-range rows were kept, none were dropped or counted differently, and endpoint coverage does not establish complete reporting.
